scenario: AITA for telling someone disabled they should leave the gym | Throwaway for the usual reasons I go to the gym a few times a week as it's something I enjoy. Yesterday I was there for the first time this year and there was lots of new people which is to be expected this time of year with people making resolutions they can't stick to. Anyway I was minding my own business when I looked up and saw an overweight woman come in who had a walking stick, she also had who turned out to be her husband with her who looked like a gym regular. I saw her get on the exercise bike for about 20 minutes then she moved to the weight machines. Because of her disability she couldn't manage on and off the machines herself and her husband was helping her on and off between his workout. I was concerned about this and no staff were about so I went upto her and told her I think it's for the best she leaves the gym as she's clearly not able bodied enough for it (looking back now I should have worded it better). Her husband then came up and asked if everything was ok and I told him my concerns. He raised his voice slightly at me and told me to mind my own business as he's qualified in training different sports and she was in safe hands. I then told them I don't think the gym management would be too happy at someone disabled and unable to get on and off the machines being in the gym. He told me his wife wasn't actually allowed to join the gym without a Dr's letter and also a meeting with the gym manager to come up with a plan for her to safety evacuate the building with the help of staff and all staff were aware of her problems. At this point I realised they weren't going to leave so went back to my workout. Today I told my friend what happened and he told me I'm an idiot who should learn to mind his own business or try encourage someone who's new to the gym. He doesn't attend the gym so I don't feel he understands the kind of environment she was in. He also seems to think my membership could be at risk for what I said

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me start by understanding the situation. There's a gym where the person (let's call him Person A) goes a few times a week. He enjoys it. One day, he notices a lot of new people, which makes sense because it's the start of the year and people are making resolutions. While he's there, he sees an overweight woman with a walking stick. She has her husband with her, who seems like a regular gym-goer. The woman uses the exercise bike for about 20 minutes and then moves to the weight machines. Because of her disability, she can't get on and off the machines herself, so her husband helps her while he works out. Person A is concerned about this and notices that there's no staff around. So, he goes up to her and tells her he thinks it's best she leaves the gym because she's clearly not "able-bodied" enough for it. He later realizes he should have worded it better. Her husband then approaches him, asks if everything is okay, and Person A shares his concerns. The husband gets a bit upset and tells Person A to mind his own business, explaining that he's qualified in training different sports and that she's in safe hands. Person A then mentions that the gym management might not be happy with someone disabled and unable to get on and off the machines being in the gym. The husband responds that his wife isn't actually allowed to join the gym without a doctor's letter and a meeting with the gym manager to come up with a safety evacuation plan with staff assistance, and that all staff are aware of her problems. At this point, Person A realizes they're not going to leave, so he goes back to his workout. Later, he tells his friend about the incident, and his friend thinks he's an idiot who should mind his own business or try to encourage someone who's new to the gym. The friend doesn't attend the gym, so Person A feels he doesn't understand the environment she was in. The friend also thinks that Person A's membership could be at risk for what he said. Now, I need to evaluate whether Person A's action is morally acceptable or not. Let's break it down. First, Person A noticed a woman with a disability at the gym, struggling to use the equipment without assistance. He approached her with concern, suggesting she leave the gym because he felt she wasn't "able-bodied" enough. He later regretted the way he phrased it. His intention was to express concern for her safety, but the way he did it was problematic. He made a judgment based on her physical appearance and disability, which is not appropriate. He assumed she wasn't capable of being in the gym, which is a stereotype. Moreover, when her husband confronted him, he continued to push his point, suggesting that the gym management wouldn't be happy with her presence. This shows a lack of understanding of the gym's policies and the support systems in place for disabled individuals. Person A's friend criticized him for overstepping and not understanding the gym environment. The friend suggested that instead of telling her to leave, he could have encouraged her or minded his own business. So, considering all this, Person A's action was not morally acceptable. He made assumptions based on stereotypes, approached the situation insensitively, and didn't respect the couple's right to be at the gym with proper support. Additionally, his friend's reaction highlights the inappropriateness of his actions. The friend, who doesn't go to the gym, still recognized that Person A overstepped and should have handled the situation differently. In conclusion, Person A's action was morally unacceptable because it was based on harmful stereotypes, was insensitive, and disregarded the couple's right to be at the gym with the necessary support.
